title: Digital Transformation and Environmental Pillar of ESG ‐Based Performance Under Financing Constraints: The Mediating Role of Green Innovation in Chinese Listed Firms
summary: ABSTRACT This study builds upon existing work that links digital transformation (DT), financing constraints (FC), green innovation (GI), and firms' environmental pillar of ESG‐based performance (SP(E)), and further examines whether DT supports SP(E) through GI under FC. Based on dynamic capabilities theory (DCT) and resource‐based view (RBV), we analyse 4456 Chinese A‐share‐listed firms during the period of 2020–2024. Two‐way fixed‐effects regression models are adopted as the main empirical approach, while generalized method of moments (GMM) estimations, two‐stage instrumental variable (IV‐2SLS) estimation, and additional robustness tests are conducted to address potential endogeneity, measurement concerns, and sensitivity issues. The results highlight that DT positively affects SP(E), and GI mediates this relationship. Particularly, the findings do not yield statistically significant evidence that FC moderate the DT–SP(E) linkage in our sample and model setting, which does not rule out the potential moderating effect of FC in other contexts. This study contributes to digital sustainability and FC research by jointly examining whether GI mediates the association between firm‐level DT and the SP(E) while simultaneously testing FC as a potential boundary condition in a panel of Chinese listed firms.

title: Research on the Impact of Green Finance on Regional Low-carbon Transformation: An Analysis of the Mediating Effect Based on Green Innovation
summary: Under the background of "double carbon" goal, green finance is an important institutional arrangement to promote green and low-carbon economic transformation. Based on China's provincial panel data from 2006 to 2023, this paper constructs a comprehensive evaluation index of green finance, and uses panel fixed effect model, mediating effect model and instrumental variable method to test the impact of green finance on regional carbon emission intensity. The results show that the development of green finance significantly reduces regional carbon emission intensity, and the conclusion is still valid after robustness test. Green finance reduces carbon emission intensity by increasing the output of green patents, and green innovation plays a complete intermediary role; Heterogeneity analysis shows that the promotion effect of green finance is more obvious in areas with low economic level and after the low-carbon policy node in 2015. This paper provides empirical evidence for improving the green finance policy system and promoting regional differentiated low-carbon development.

title: Digital Transformation, Carbon Disclosure and Firm Performance: The Moderating Role of Green Innovation in European Listed Firms
summary: ABSTRACT In the context of accelerating digital and sustainability transitions, firms increasingly face the strategic challenge of simultaneously enhancing technological capabilities and environmental transparency. This study examines the associations of digital transformation and carbon disclosure with firm performance and investigates whether green innovation moderates these relationships in European listed firms. Using a panel dataset of 510 non‐financial firms from the STOXX Europe 600 over the period 2015–2023, the study employs dynamic system GMM estimations complemented by extensive robustness analyses, including winsorized regressions, quantile regressions, nonlinear specifications, sub‐sample analyses, cross‐sectional dependence corrections, and alternative specifications. The findings reveal that digital transformation and carbon disclosure are positively associated with firm performance. The results further indicate that green innovation significantly strengthens these relationships, suggesting that environmentally oriented innovation capabilities enhance the value creation potential of digital and sustainability strategies. Additional evidence shows that the positive effects of digital transformation and carbon disclosure are more pronounced at higher levels of digital transformation, in carbon‐intensive industries, and among firms in upper‐performance quantiles. This study contributes to the emerging literature on digital sustainability by integrating digital transformation, carbon disclosure, and green innovation into a unified empirical framework. The findings highlight the strategic complementarities between technological and environmental capabilities and provide important implications for managers and policymakers seeking to align digital transition objectives with sustainable business development and long‐term value creation.

title: Environmental strategy and digital transformation: pathways to green innovation and sustainable performance in Vietnamese manufacturing firms
summary: Abstract Manufacturing firms in emerging economies face dual pressures to improve both environmental performance and digital technology adoption. Both themes have attracted extensive research attention on their own, yet few studies ask whether—and through what mechanisms—a proactive environmental strategy is associated with a stronger orientation toward both digital transformation and green innovation as parallel routes to sustainable performance. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study develops and tests an integrated model in which proactive environmental strategy is examined as an organisational-level antecedent associated with digital transformation and green innovation among Vietnamese manufacturing firms. Data from 602 manufacturing enterprises were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. Proactive environmental strategy is positively associated with both digital transformation and green innovation, and each of these, in turn, is positively associated with sustainable performance—a pattern consistent with partial mediation. Four antecedents predict proactive environmental strategy: organisational support, dynamic environment, green transformational leadership, and stakeholder pressure. One notable null result stands out: industry type (resource-intensive versus high-technology) does not moderate the environmental-strategy-to-digital-transformation link, so this relationship appears stable across manufacturing contexts. The study contributes to theory by jointly integrating the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory to explain how environmental strategy is converted into digital and innovation-based capabilities, and it offers evidence that digital transformation and green innovation function as parallel, comparably weighted mediating pathways rather than competing mechanisms in an emerging-economy manufacturing context.

title: Digital Economy Policy and National Competitiveness: Nigeria and China in Perspective
summary: The study compared the digital economy policies of Nigeria and China to examine how differences in policy design influence national competitiveness. Specifically, it analysed Nigeria’s National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy (NDEPS 2020–2030) and China’s Digital China Construction Overall Layout Plan (2023–2035) with a view to understanding their institutional structures, governance arrangements, and implementation models. Guided by Policy Capacity Theory, the study adopted a qualitative method through a comparative policy analysis, drawing on official policy documents, government reports, and relevant scholarly literature. It was found that Nigeria’s digital economy strategy is largely market-driven and relies on private sector participation, public-private partnerships, and external financing. This approach contributed to improvements in digital inclusion, broadband expansion, and fintech development, challenges relating to institutional coordination, infrastructure gaps, and limited public investment constrain competitiveness. China’s strategy built around centralised coordination, state-directed financing, and long-term technological planning enabled the country to develop advanced digital infrastructure, strengthen innovation capacity, and position itself as a leading actor in emerging technologies. The study concluded that national competitiveness in the digital economy is shaped not only by the existence of digital policies but also by the coherence of policy design, governance structures, and implementation capacity. It therefore recommended that Nigeria strengthen institutional coordination, improve strategic public investment in digital infrastructure, and develop a more integrated framework for long-term digital transformation.

title: Transportation Safety, and Supply Chain Resilience in Road-Based Crude Oil Logistics: Evidence from a Conflict‐Affected Region
summary: Abstract Crude oil transport is a vital component of global energy supply chains; however, it is riddled with systemic risks, including human error, infrastructure fragility, security vulnerabilities, and regulatory deficiencies. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of crude oil transport, with particular emphasis on the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRG), a semi-autonomous territory that has emerged as a significant oil producer despite enduring geopolitical instability. By triangulating peer-reviewed literature, industry reports, regulatory documents, and primary survey data from 150 public respondents and 50 tanker drivers and owners within the KRG, this study articulates the multifaceted risks associated with road-based crude oil transport. Economic regression analysis, employing logistic regression, difference-in-differences, and ordered probit models, reveals that regular safety training reduces the odds of an accident by 58.4% (p=0.005); the 2023-2025 KRG-Turkey pipeline suspension caused approximately $12.5 billion in economic losses; and pipeline resumption increased realised prices by 38.50 per barrel (p<0.001). Key findings indicate that public awareness of transport risks is moderate, with only 11% expressing high confidence in regulatory oversight; 73% of respondents identified tanker accidents as their primary environmental concern; 46% of drivers reported experiencing accidents, while 74% witnessed spills or leaks; infrastructure deficits, including poor road conditions reported by 68% of drivers and inadequate equipment, constitute primary operational hazards; and geopolitical disruptions aggravate safety vulnerabilities by increasing reliance on higher-risk road transport. Cost-benefit analysis indicates that driver training programmes and GPS tracking mandates yield benefit-cost ratios of 25.4:1 and 25.7:1, respectively. The paper proposes a novel analytical framework that integrates human factors, security threats, and regulatory responses, offering evidence-based recommendations for policy reform in conflict-affected oil-producing regions.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility in India: A Legal Examination
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is defined by the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014, as amended in 2021, as “the activities undertaken by a Company in pursuance of its statutory obligation laid down in section 135 of the Act”. In simple terms, Corporate Social Responsibility means that companies have a duty to contribute ethically and positively to society while conducting their business. Corporate Social Responsibility draws on the Triple Bottom Line approach, which measures a company’s success along three dimensions, people, planet and profit, and not by financial gain alone. This article examines Corporate Social Responsibility from a legal perspective, discussing its evolution and how it is treated under Indian law. It also explains the role of law in promoting Corporate Social Responsibility, why companies should engage in Corporate Social Responsibility activities, and the challenges faced in implementing and enforcing Corporate Social Responsibility.

title: Development of logistics 4.0 efficiency indicators system in supply chain management
summary: The study aims to develop an integrated system of key performance indicators (KPIs) to evaluate digital logistics processes in Industry 4.0 conditions. The research is relevant because traditional performance measurement systems must adapt to the specifics of digital supply chain transformation and the growing importance of sustainability metrics in modern business operations. The methodology is based on systematic analysis of modern scientific approaches to supply chain performance measurement, adaptation of the Balanced Scorecard framework with integration of a fifth sustainability perspective, and mathematical modeling for logistics efficiency forecasting using the Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) method with a modified range-adjusted measure. The results include the development of a comprehensive multi-level KPI system covering operational indicators (order cycle time, picking accuracy, inventory turnover, digital integration index), financial metrics (logistics costs per unit, investment ROI, transportation costs per ton-kilometer), environmental indicators (carbon footprint, energy efficiency, waste management, recycling coefficient), and customer-oriented metrics (on-time delivery rate, order fill rate, customer satisfaction index, Net Promoter Score). We propose and empirically validate a mathematical model to forecast logistics process efficiency using a modified DEA-MRAM method with a digitalization impact coefficient. The scientific novelty lies in creating an integrated framework for Logistics 4.0 assessment that combines traditional metrics with digital maturity and sustainability indicators; systematizing sustainability indicators for logistics systems across three Triple Bottom Line dimensions (environmental, social, economic); and adapting the MRAM-DEA mathematical model with the integration of the digitalization impact coefficient, which allows quantitative assessment of digital transformation effects on operational performance. The practical significance lies in applying the developed KPI system to diagnose and optimize enterprise logistics processes across industries amid economic digital transformation and ESG reporting requirements. The developed implementation methodology includes four sequential stages: diagnostics, design, implementation, and monitoring using the PDCA continuous improvement cycle. Future research should empirically validate the KPI system in Ukrainian enterprises, develop industry-specific framework adaptations for different economic sectors, and investigate the impact of geopolitical factors on logistics system efficiency. Keywords: Logistics 4.0, key performance indicators, supply chain, digital transformation, balanced scorecard, sustainable development, DEA analysis, digital maturity.

title: Stakeholder perceptions of seafood supply chain resilience and sustainability: an Australian case study
summary: Abstract Seafood supply chains face increasing disruption from climate change, pandemics, and changing market conditions, creating challenges for maintaining both resilience and sustainability. Understanding the perspectives of people working in the industry and supply chain (i.e. stakeholders) are crucial to developing context-specific and practical pathways for supporting continued seafood supply, livelihoods and profitability. Our study examines how supply chain stakeholders (e.g., producers, processors, exporters, retailers, industry representatives and researchers) perceive resilience and sustainability across three Australian seafood supply chains: edible oysters, rock lobster and barramundi. Drawing on a qualitative survey of 102 stakeholders, we identify key patterns in how these concepts are understood and operationalised in addition to perceived disruptions, challenges, opportunities, and adaptive capacity. Most participants perceived their seafood supply chains as both resilient and sustainable, despite recent major disruptions. Stakeholders attributed resilience and sustainability primarily to economic stability (supply, demand, profitability), effective governance (fisheries management and regulation), environmentally responsible and sustainable production practices and adaptive capacity (e.g. adapting to market changes and having flexible logistics). Importantly, resilience was reinforced by adaptive behaviours, including learning from past disruptions, collaboration, and information sharing across supply chain actors. While sustainability was commonly associated with reducing environmental impacts and maintaining economic viability, social dimensions were underrepresented, revealing a gap between stakeholder perceptions and broader socio-ecological sustainability frameworks. Based on these findings, we develop a framework linking disruptions, challenges, opportunities, and data needs to support decision-making and preparedness. Although focused on Australia, the findings provide transferable insights for strengthening resilience and sustainability in seafood supply chains globally.

title: How conversational AI shapes the readability of 10-K reports
summary: Purpose We investigate whether the adoption of conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) translates corporate complexity into clearer financial narratives. CAI, representing AI-driven innovation, can bolster operational efficiency and performance, thereby leading to better financial transparency and readability of financial statement information. Design/methodology/approach We construct a firm-level CAI measure from CAI-related disclosures in 10-K filings using Sent-latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA)-variational expectation maximization (VEM) topic modelling. Our measure captures CAI applications related to service and operations, and decision-making and governance. We also use patent-based measures based on natural language processing and speech-recognition technologies as alternative proxies in robustness tests. Findings We find that CAI adoption is associated with lower Bog Index scores, indicating more readable 10-K reports. Mediation tests show that financial performance and operational efficiency partially mediate this relationship. The results remain robust after addressing endogeneity concerns and using alternative specifications. Originality/value Using unsupervised machine learning topic modelling, we observe that CAI is predominantly employed in corporate operations, notably in service-related activities, decision-making processes and corporate governance.

title: Smart policy, green innovation: The mediation role of environmental regulation
summary: Digitalization has become a key enabler for sustainable transformation, as it increases technological capacity, optimizes resource use and facilitates green innovation. This study examines the link between digitalization, environmental regulations, and green innovation by employing a cross-country panel data set from OECD and World Bank sources for the period 2004–2022. The study uses Structural Equation Modeling to analyze the direct and indirect relationships between digitalization, environmental regulations, and green innovation. Fixed Effects, Panel Corrected Standard Errors and Driscoll-Kraay estimations further validate the robustness of the findings. The results indicate that digitalization is an important key factor of sustainable technological advancement and that it has a significant impact on green innovation. Moreover, the results illustrate that the relationship between digitalization and green innovation is mediated positively by environmental regulations, which underscore that the environmental regulations enhance the impact of digitalization on green innovation. The findings of this study have important policy implications because it shows that to enhance green innovation, environmental policies need to be digitally enabled and incentive based. Future research could build on this analysis by examining sector-specific impacts, other digitalization dimensions, and the influence of institutional factors on sustainable innovation outcomes.

title: Capital Market Opening-up and High-Quality Innovation of Enterprises
summary: At present, China’s innovation field is facing the structural dilemma of quantity priority and insufficient quality. In the critical window period when the economy turns to high-quality development, the improvement of enterprise innovation level has become an important issue. Based on the quasi-natural experimental scenario of capital market opening, this paper constructs a multi-period difference-in-differences model to test the effect of capital market opening on the quality of enterprise innovation. Both theoretical deduction and empirical test show that capital market opening helps to improve the quality of enterprise innovation, and this effect is more significant in state-owned enterprises and enterprises with overseas business income. From the perspective of mechanism, on the one hand, the opening of capital market promotes the improvement of innovation quality by improving corporate governance and alleviating financing bottlenecks ; on the other hand, due to the increase of stock liquidity, the quality of innovation is suppressed. Overall, the positive effect is dominant. This paper not only expands the theoretical analysis of the relationship between capital market opening and enterprise innovation, but also provides a useful reference for policy practice.

title: Managing supplier risk through procurement decisions: a decision-making framework for the automotive industry
summary: Purpose Automotive supply chains face increasing exposure to supplier-related disruptions, yet existing frameworks inadequately integrate risk categorisation, procurement decision-making, and supply chain resilience into a unified decision-support structure. This study addresses that challenge by developing and validating a theory-grounded supplier risk decision-making framework for procurement managers in the automotive industry. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review (SLR) of peer-reviewed publications was conducted to synthesise supplier risk typologies and procurement decision frameworks. The resulting framework was subsequently validated through structured interviews with automotive industry experts to ensure practical applicability and managerial relevance. Findings This study presents a comprehensive supplier risk categorisation comprising six major risk types and thirty-seven contributing factors. Procurement decisions are organised into three groups: supplier categorisation, supplier performance management, and supplier relationship management. A novel supplier risk decision-making framework, grounded in prescriptive decision theory and informed by contingency theory, delineates strategic, tactical and operational decision-making stages to support effective supplier risk mitigation. Practical implications The framework has been adopted by a leading UK automotive manufacturer to train procurement professionals, providing evidence of its practical relevance and real-world applicability. Social implications The framework contributes to more stable and resilient automotive supply chains, supporting business continuity and reducing the broader economic disruptions associated with supplier failures in a sector of considerable economic importance. Originality/value The proposed framework integrates supplier risk management, supply chain resilience and procurement decisions, offering a holistic foundation for effective and informed decision-making.

title: Corporate Transparency and Disclosure Obligations in India
summary: Efficient disclosure methods ensure that investors obtain precise, prompt and thorough information about the financial status, governance framework and operational activities of companies. In India, corporate transparency and disclosure obligations secure accountability through mandatory reporting under the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. These rules promote investor trust by requiring timely financial statements, annual reporting, a governance framework and ESG disclosures. This paper examines the legal provisions governing corporate disclosure in India under the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, and assesses the role of the Securities and Exchange Board of India in promoting transparency and safeguarding investors. It offers an examination of investor protection, corporate responsibility and transparency in the Indian capital markets, analyses the extent to which corporate disclosure practices protect investors' interests and enhance market transparency, and identifies issues and gaps in the existing disclosure system. The research also examines the effects of insufficient disclosure on investor trust.

title: Heterogeneous effects of bottom-up responsiveness and top-down central environmental inspection on corporate green innovation across ownership and competition
summary: This paper examines how bottom-up municipal responsiveness and top-down central environmental inspection pressure shape firms' green innovation behavior in China. Using a firm-level panel of all non-financial A-listed firms, patent data from the China Research Data Services Platform, a city-level government responsiveness index, and the first round of Central Environmental Protection Inspections, we study how different environmental governance pressures are associated with green innovation in firms’ overall innovation portfolios. To address endogeneity in municipal responsiveness, we use an instrumental-variable strategy based on lagged leave-one-out responsiveness of other cities within the same province. To examine central inspection pressure, we combine province-cohort exposure regressions with double/debiased machine learning, recognizing that all provinces were eventually inspected and that the design therefore lacks a conventional never-treated control group. The results are consistent with a dual-channel pattern. Municipal responsiveness is positively associated with firms' green innovation share mainly in the contemporaneous specification and among non-SOEs (state-owned enterprises), consistent with a bottom-up local governance-signaling mechanism. By contrast, central inspection exposure is associated with a stronger green innovation response among SOEs, consistent with a top-down political accountability mechanism. For non-SOEs, market competition weakens the conversion of central inspection exposure into green innovation. These findings suggest that environmental governance does not affect firms’ innovation behavior uniformly: its association with green innovation depends on the level of government from which pressure originates, the ownership structure of the firm, and the competitive environment in which the firm operates.

title: Climate Finance and State Capacity in Africa: Institutional Constraints on Climate-Policy Implementation
summary: The financing of climate change in Africa has become the focus of climate change policy implementation, since most African nations have significant adaptation and mitigation needs and are experiencing low-carbon development, and are constrained by limited fiscal resources. However, access to finance is not enough to ensure good policy implementation. This article explores the linkage between climate finance and state capacity in Africa, detailing the constraints that shape a State's capacity to mobilise, access, allocate, execute, monitor and account for climate-related financial resources. The article concludes that Africa's climate policy implementation issue is a financing issue and a state capacity issue, based on evidence compiled from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the African Development Bank (AfDB), the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank, Climate Policy Institute (CPI), the OECD and recent peer-reviewed research. African countries are also burdened with challenges on how to prepare projects, public financial management, intergovernmental coordination, data systems, institutional mandates, monitoring and evaluation, and fiduciary and technical needs of international climate funds. Experience in Ghana, Uganda, Nigeria, Kenya, Rwanda, and Africa in general has shown that the establishment of a formal climate plan and legislation often outpaces the institutional structures and processes needed to execute it. The article instead theorises the climate finance as a tool for governance that is only effective in its development according to how well the institution can absorb it. It finds that scaling up climate finance in Africa needs to be accompanied by a simultaneous reform of domestic fiscal systems, the process of project preparation, climate budgeting, public investment management, coordination, subnational capacity, monitoring, and direct access to international climate funds.

title: A hybrid simulation-optimization decision (HySOD) framework for resilient and sustainable supply chain management
summary: Global supply chains face increasing exposure to demand volatility, capacity constraints, and transportation disruptions, yet existing frameworks struggle to ensure both mathematical optimality and operational feasibility under real-world conditions. Optimization models generate prescriptive solutions without guaranteeing executability, while simulation models capture operational realism but lack prescriptive power. This study addresses this gap by developing and validating HySOD (Hybrid Simulation-Optimization Decision). This closed-loop simulation-based optimization system integrates Mixed-Integer Linear Programming with a multi-method simulation platform combining system dynamics, agent-based modelling, and discrete-event simulation. The framework embeds optimizer-generated shipment allocations as runtime parameters within the simulation environment, applies an evolutionary multi-objective algorithm for Pareto-optimal resilience strategy identification, and employs Monte Carlo testing for stochastic robustness validation, all executed against 14 weeks of real factory-warehouse-customer operational data. Statistical validation across 30 replications confirmed significant improvements over the baseline: service level rose from 85.1% to 90.0%, stockout rate fell by 46%, the resilience index improved by seven percentage points, and total cost decreased modestly. Three primary contributions are made: a closed-loop simulation-optimization architecture; a tri-layer linear programming model producing auditable, directly executable shipment plans; and a systematic Pareto-based evaluation: buffer stock, just-in-time scheduling, flexible manufacturing, redundant routing, and dynamic pricing under stochastic supply chain disruptions. The findings demonstrate that bridging mathematical optimization with operational simulation produces supply chain decisions that are simultaneously cost-efficient, executable, and resilient.

title: Toward Evidence‐Based ESG Reporting: The Added Value of Geospatial and Satellite Data
summary: ABSTRACT This study addresses the limitations of conventional ESG reporting, including reliance on self‐reported and third‐party data, lack of standardization, and limited verifiability, by examining how geospatial data enhance disclosure quality. It aims to synthesize and critically evaluate existing research on satellite and geospatial data in ESG reporting in order to identify dominant research directions and unresolved challenges. It employs a systematic bibliometric analysis of Scopus‐indexed publications, complemented by thematic mapping and cluster identification, to explore the structure and evolution of the literature. The findings demonstrate that geospatial data enhance environmental performance measurement, enable asset‐level monitoring, and strengthen risk assessment, thereby mitigating information asymmetries. Nevertheless, the diffusion of these data remains constrained by coverage gaps, methodological inconsistencies, and governance issues. Standardization and interoperability challenges can be tackled through stronger global governance and structured public‐private collaboration that aligns data production with concrete user needs in sustainable finance, agriculture, and environmental management.

title: Local creative culture environment and corporate digital transformation: evidence from cultural and creative industry parks in China
summary: Based on a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we investigate the influence of the local creative culture environment on corporate digital transformation (DT). The results show that a vibrant creative culture environment is positively related to firms’ DT, primarily through three channels: higher R&D investments, lower financing constraints and higher regional digital talent agglomeration. Moreover, heterogeneity analyses reveal that this effect is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, in regions with weaker Confucian cultural traditions, and in firms with a higher proportion of female executives. We enhance the literature on the drivers of DT from the perspective of the local creative culture environment. The findings also provide policy implications for promoting the synergies between cultural development and the digital economy.

title: Building Circular Economy Capabilities: A Systematic Review of Drivers, Practices, Digital Enablers, and Sustainable Outcomes
summary: This study aims to analyze the development of circular economy capabilities and explain the driving factors, organizational capabilities, circular practices, and sustainability outcomes that are relevant to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The research uses a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) combined with bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed publications for the 2010-2026 period. The initial search yielded 402,309 documents. After the process of checking and eliminating duplication in the selected dataset, 35 unique articles were obtained, with 20 articles explicitly discussing the circular economy, circularity, circular supply chain, or circular business model. The results show that circular economy capabilities are not formed as a single ability, but develop through the interaction between innovation capabilities, collaboration, digitalization, knowledge management, governance, and organizational capabilities. Digitalization plays an enabling role that strengthens the implementation of circular practices when supported by organizational readiness and strategic capabilities. Practices identified include resource use reduction, reuse, material recovery, recycling, circular design, backflow management, and circular business model development. The research synthesis resulted in an integrative framework driving → circular economy capabilities → circular practices → sustainable outcomes. Sustainable outcomes include improved resource efficiency, waste and emissions reduction, supply chain resilience, economic performance, and business resilience. This study expands the understanding of the circular economy from a practice-based approach to an organizational capability perspective and shows that empirical evidence specifically addressing MSMEs is still limited, opening up space for further research.

title: Digital corporate responsibility as an element of corporate social responsibility (a case study of Ukrainian agricultural enterprises)
summary: The article aims to substantiate the theoretical, methodological, and practical foundations of Digital Corporate Responsibility (DCR/CDR) as a direction of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) amid the comprehensive digitalization of business processes, focusing on Ukraine’s agricultural sector. The study applies dialectical analysis and synthesis, grouping, structural-functional analysis, and case study methods. The results show that digitalization creates significant opportunities to improve the efficiency, productivity, and profitability of agribusiness while generating new ethical, social, and environmental risks, including cybersecurity threats, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, the carbon footprint of IT infrastructure, and electronic waste. DCR is therefore considered an important mechanism for mitigating these risks and ensuring socially and environmentally responsible digital transformation. The scientific novelty lies in substantiating DCR within three interrelated ESG dimensions: digital environmental (E), digital social (S), and digital governance (G) responsibility. The study shows that implementing DCR can strengthen stakeholder relations, transparency, trust, and the sustainable development potential of agricultural companies. The experience of leading Ukrainian agricultural holdings, including Astarta and Kernel, illustrates practical approaches to combining digital technologies with responsible business practices. The research’s practical significance lies in the proposed use of corporate digital ethics codes to strengthen cybersecurity, protect digital rights, develop digital culture, and promote responsible digital behavior among employees and stakeholders. Further research should focus on developing a comprehensive system of indicators to assess the level of DCR, identifying relevant ESG criteria, and adapting international approaches and best practices to the institutional and socio-economic conditions of Ukrainian agribusiness. title: Artificial Intelligence-enabled value creation and competitive advantage in supply chain management: A dynamic capabilities perspective
summary: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) creates strategic value in supply chain management (SCM) by integrating technological capabilities, organizational agility, and human expertise. Using a mixed-methods design, the study combines quantitative survey data from 250 global supply chain executives with three qualitative industry case studies to develop the Artificial Intelligence–Supply Chain Management (AI-SCM) Value Creation Framework, grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory. Organizations with higher AI maturity reported 31.5% higher demand-forecast accuracy and 14.5% lower logistics and freight costs. Qualitative evidence indicates that AI-enabled predictive analytics, adaptive decision-making, and operational integration can strengthen supply chain agility and resilience. AI can function as an embedded strategic capability when supported by organizational readiness, reliable data, and human expertise. However, these benefits are not unconditional. Environmental burdens associated with AI infrastructure and algorithmic management risks, including surveillance and reduced worker autonomy, require responsible governance and meaningful human oversight. AI-enabled value creation is therefore contingent on technological capability, organizational conditions, and responsible human-AI integration. title: CAPITAL STRUCTURE AND LIQUIDITY ON FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE: THE MODERATING ROLE OF GOOD CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
summary: The phenomenon of fluctuating financial performance in companies listed in the LQ45 index in Indonesia remains a concern, as indicated by changes in Net Profit Margin (NPM). This condition is influenced by internal factors such as capital structure, liquidity, and the implementation of good corporate governance that has not yet been optimal. This study aims to analyze the effect of capital structure and liquidity on financial performance with good corporate governance as a moderating variable. The data used are secondary data obtained from financial statements and annual reports of 20 LQ45 index companies during the 2022–2024 period. The analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model (REM) through EViews 12. The results of this study indicate that capital structure and liquidity have a significant effect on financial performance. In addition, good corporate governance is able to moderate the effect of capital structure and liquidity on financial performance. The implications of this study emphasize the importance of optimal capital structure and liquidity management, as well as strengthening corporate governance to support the improvement of financial performance. This study is expected to serve as a consideration for company management and investors in making more effective and sustainable decisions.

title: The Effect of Simulation-Based Internal Audit Engagements on Digital Competence and Professional Scepticism Among Auditing Students
summary: Digital transformation imperatives have resulted in many organisations migrating to digital spaces, to ensure they remain competitive. This has led to the shift of skills and competencies that are required from auditors. With this background, the study sought to assess the effects of simulation-based internal audit engagements on digital competence and professional scepticism among auditing students. This study is theoretically grounded in competence-based education (CBE). The study has employed mixed-research approach, questionnaire, student reflective journal and focused group interviews were used as a data collection tool. The data was collected form 98 students form a selected university that offers simulation-based auditing engagements. The study revealed that simulation-based internal audit engagements are an effective pedagogical strategy for preparing students for the modern auditing profession. The results further demonstrated that simulation-based auditing engagements significantly improves both digital competence and professional scepticism. These two competencies are increasingly recognised as essential for auditors operating in technologically complex environments. The study contributes to auditing education literature by providing empirical evidence supporting simulation-based pedagogies in developing future-ready internal auditors. The findings have implications for curriculum transformation, accreditation standards, and the integration of technology-enhanced learning within auditing programmes.

title: Opportunities and risks of ESG factors in early-stage ventures: evidence from the software sector
summary: Abstract Early-stage software startups face increasing pressure to integrate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles, yet most research on ESG performance focuses on established, publicly listed firms. This study examines how ESG creates opportunities and risks for nascent software ventures and how its role changes across funding stages. We employ a qualitative interview study combining semi-structured interviews with representatives of German software startups and venture capital investors, complemented by document analysis. Using a content-structuring approach, we analyze how entrepreneurs and investors perceive, implement, and evaluate ESG practices. Findings show that ESG functions primarily as a hygiene factor in early venture stages, supporting credibility with customers, employees, and regulators. Around the transition from seed to Series A, ESG takes on a signaling role as investor attention rises through limited-partner mandates and sustainability screening. Internal ESG practices are typically secondary to a product’s external impact unless required by due diligence or regulation. Startups report opportunities in cost control, risk management, and sales enablement, but also risks in symbolic compliance and misalignment with growth priorities. We interpret these findings through a stage-sensitive lens that distinguishes hygiene and signaling logics and highlights an investor bifurcation between impact-oriented and financially driven funds, shaped by limited partner mandates, due diligence requirements, and stage-specific expectations. The study refines boundary conditions in the ESG–performance debate and offers practical guidance for aligning ESG practices with venture maturity.

title: Staged digital transformation and firms’ total factor productivity: evidence from Chinese cultural firms
summary: This study explores the effects of digital transformation (DT) on firms’ total factor productivity (TFP) across the digital technology application (DTA) stage and digital business model innovation (DBMI) stage. Using a sample of 245 Chinese listed cultural firms from 2011 to 2022, we examine how DT impacts TFP differently across these stages. The results show that DT significantly enhances firms’ TFP in both the DTA and DBMI stages. However, productivity gains materialize only after firms reach the transformation threshold in both stages. Moreover, the threshold for the DTA stage is higher than that for the DBMI stage. In the DTA stage, DT improves firms’ TFP by enhancing their core production capabilities and specialization. In the DBMI stage, DT affects firms’ TFP through improved operational efficiency and financial efficiency. Furthermore, during the DTA stage, larger firms experience stronger TFP gains, while smaller firms benefit more in the DBMI stage. In the DTA stage, the positive impact of DT on TFP is similar for firms with and without government subsidies. In the DBMI stage, however, the impact of DT is more pronounced for firms without subsidies. Across both stages, firms in regions with a better digital financial environment achieve greater productivity gains from DT.

title: Systematization of the components of the digital transformation mechanism for managing national economic development
summary: The article examines the theoretical foundations for developing a digital transformation mechanism to manage national economic development. The article summarizes existing scholarly approaches to interpreting the concept of a “mechanism,” with particular attention to its systemic and process-oriented nature and its specific application in the context of digital transformation. The article analyzes contemporary approaches to defining and structuring digital transformation mechanisms at different levels of governance, enabling identification of differences in their structural composition, functional purpose, and logic of interaction. The concept of a “digital transformation mechanism for managing the development of the national economy” is refined with due regard to the systemic nature of digital transformation, its strategic orientation, and the interdependence of its components. The study supports systematizing the mechanism’s components by functional purpose. It proposes distinguishing institutional, organizational, financial and economic, technological, human resources, and analytical mechanisms. The study defines their functional purposes and complementary nature in implementing digital transformation processes. The effectiveness of the mechanism depends on the coherence of interaction among its components and their capacity to ensure the achievement of the strategic goals of national economic development. The importance of analytical support for monitoring, performance assessment, identifying deviations, and adjusting managerial decisions is emphasized, thereby creating a feedback loop within the digital transformation process. The proposed systematization provides a basis for further specifying the instrumental content of individual components of the mechanism, identifying their relationship with the strategic goals of digital transformation, and assessing the effectiveness of digital transformation processes. title: THE CIRCULAR CREATIVE ECONOMY: SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN COMMERCIAL PHOTOGRAPHY AND DESIGN PRODUCTION
summary: Global economic uncertainty and the climate crisis demand fundamental transformations across various sectors, including the creative industry. Conventional commercial photography and visual communication design production often generate a substantial carbon footprint through material waste, excessive energy consumption, and high logistical mobility. This paper explores the integration of circular economy principles and digital transformation within visual production workflows as a strategic response to these sustainability challenges. This research aims to analyze how the adoption of disruptive technologies - such as generative artificial intelligence, virtual production, and cloud computing - can reduce carbon emissions while simultaneously enhancing operational cost efficiency. The methodology employs a systematic literature review alongside qualitative case studies of creative agencies that have implemented sustainable workflows. Findings indicate that the digitalization of creative processes effectively eliminates physical waste, notably excessive sample printing and single-use practical set constructions. Furthermore, the transition toward a virtual production ecosystem is proven to drastically minimize logistical expenses, thereby bolstering the financial resilience of industry practitioners amidst a fragmented global economy. Leveraging cutting-edge technology also substantially accelerates project turnaround times without compromising aesthetic design quality. In conclusion, the adoption of digital technologies is not merely a fleeting aesthetic trend but an essential catalyst for establishing a circular and inclusive creative economy. This innovative transformation empowers visual communication designers and professional photographers to remain productive, relevant, and highly competitive globally. Ultimately, these crucial economic milestones can be achieved while practitioners uphold strong ethical responsibilities toward ecological preservation and the development of future-proof business models.

title: Rural E-Commerce and rural revitalization: the income channel and the complementary role of FinTech
summary: Against the strategic imperative of rural revitalization in China, this study examines how rural e-commerce contributes to rural revitalization and whether financial technology (FinTech) strengthens this relationship. Baseline regressions show a significant positive association between rural e-commerce and rural revitalization, and the result remains robust to an alternative measure of rural e-commerce, clustered standard errors, a restricted sample, and an instrumental-variable approach. Mechanism analysis shows that rural e-commerce significantly increases household income, supporting the proposed income channel. FinTech also strengthens the positive association between e-commerce and rural revitalization: the interaction terms for overall FinTech development, coverage breadth, usage depth, and digitalization are positive and statistically significant. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the e-commerce coefficient is statistically significant in villages with larger household bases, greater land area, and larger labour forces. These findings provide empirical evidence on the complementarity between digital commerce and financial services in rural development and offer policy implications for inclusive, digitally enabled rural revitalization.

title: Audit Committee Size and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Non-Financial Firms in Nigeria
summary: Main purpose: This study examined the effect of audit committee size on the financial reporting quality of non-financial firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX). Methodology: Secondary data were obtained from the annual reports of 58 sampled non-financial firms, drawn from a population of 106 listed firms, covering the period from 2013 to 2024. The data were analysed using panel regression estimation techniques to determine the effect of audit committee size and relevant firm-specific variables on financial reporting quality. Findings: The results revealed that audit committee size had a positive and statistically significant effect on financial reporting quality (t = 2.2511, p < 0.05), indicating that larger audit committees may provide broader oversight of the financial reporting process. Leverage also had a positive and statistically significant effect on financial reporting quality (t = 2.0864, p < 0.05). In contrast, audit firm size had a negative and statistically significant association with financial reporting quality (t = −3.1325, p < 0.05), suggesting that the use of larger audit firms does not necessarily translate into higher financial reporting quality among the sampled firms. Practical implications: Boards of listed non-financial firms should maintain appropriately constituted audit committees with sufficient membership and members possessing relevant financial and accounting expertise to strengthen oversight of the financial reporting process. Corporate boards and regulators should also pay closer attention to audit committee composition, leverage practices and the effectiveness of external audit arrangements rather than relying solely on audit firm size as an indicator of reporting quality. Originality/novelty: This study extends the Nigerian corporate governance literature by applying Shivakumar’s (2003) accounting-quality model to examine the effect of audit committee size on financial reporting quality among listed non-financial firms, thereby providing context-specific evidence from a segment characterised by distinct regulatory and governance frameworks. title: From State Financial Loss to Investment Risk: Reconstructing State Financial Accountability in SOEs Management Based on Fairness and Sustainable Governance
summary: State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) play a strategic role in national economic development. Yet, their investment management is constrained by the coexistence of the result-based liability paradigm under Law No. 17 of 2003 and the risk-based governance paradigm introduced by Article 3H of Law No. 16 of 2025. This regulatory disharmony creates legal uncertainty that discourages directors from making strategic investment decisions because commercially reasonable investments may be criminalized when they fail. This study examines the paradigm shift in state financial accountability and reconstructs an accountability model grounded in fairness and sustainable governance. Employing normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and philosophical approaches, the study analyzes legislation, Constitutional Court decisions, legal doctrines, and relevant literature. The findings demonstrate that investment losses should not automatically be classified as state financial losses. Instead, they should be recognized as ordinary business risks, provided investment decisions are made in good faith, with due care, free from conflicts of interest, and in accordance with the principles of Good Corporate Governance and the Business Judgment Rule. Accordingly, legal accountability should focus on the integrity of the decision-making process rather than solely on financial outcomes. The proposed reconstruction ensures fairness by protecting directors who act professionally and in good faith from unjust criminal prosecution while preserving accountability for managerial negligence and corrupt conduct. This study introduces an investment risk-based state financial accountability model that harmonizes state finance law, SOE law, corporate law, and anti-corruption law by integrating the Business Judgment Rule, fiduciary duty, enterprise risk management, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles. The study’s novelty lies in developing a coherent governance framework that distinguishes business risk from negligence and corruption, strengthens legal certainty, promotes sustainable governance, and supports more competitive and innovative SOEs.

title: Climate Change Act Implementation in Nigeria: State Capacity and Institutional Coordination, 2021–2025
summary: The Climate Change Act 2021 is Nigeria's first statute that provides a comprehensive coordination framework for climate-change mitigation and adaptation, climate finance, carbon management and mainstreaming of climate action at the national level across government and the wider economy. The Act also set up the National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), established a dedicated Secretariat, established the Climate Change Fund, implemented carbon-budgeting mechanisms and mandated the creation of a National Climate Change Action Plan. Thus, its implementation in the years of 2021-2025 offers a valuable case study for the study of the relationship between legal institutionalization and state capacity and policy implementation in a federal developing state. The article does this by documentary evidence drawn from the Climate Change Act, Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) of Nigeria, National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), the World Bank (WB), the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and related peer-reviewed scholarly works during the period under evaluation. It is centred on four pillars of state capacity: institutional capacity, coordination capacity, technical and information capacity and financial and enforcement capacity. The evidence suggests that there was significant institutional development in Nigeria over the period. The NCCC became the highest-level climate body, a new Secretariat was created, the national planning process was more closely linked to climate, the NDC was enhanced, the Energy Transition Plan was put together, and the climate finance machinery was further developed, while national agencies were increasingly involved in climate data and planning processes. But implementation was not uniform. The statutory architecture is more sophisticated and difficult to operationalize in any coordinated, measurable and enforceable manner at ministerial, departmental, agency, state and local levels. Challenges encompassed institutional mandates that overlap, inadequate vertical coordination, limited data and monitoring, domestic climate finance limitations, reliance on external technical support, subnational capacity gaps, as well as the trade-offs between climate and Nigeria's fiscal and hydrocarbon energy reliance. The article states that the challenge for the principal implementation during 2021–2025 was not the lack of climate policy but the mismatch between a policy framework and the state capacity to implement it. This needs to be supported by more effective intergovernmental coordination, shared accountability, integrated monitoring and verification frameworks, climate finance predictability and increased institutional capacity at subnational and local levels.

title: Looking for love in the wrong place: why marketers should focus on management accounting
summary: Purpose Marketers and marketing academics are frustrated that the contribution of marketing to business success is inadequately represented in financial accounts. This study explains how marketers' interests are misaligned with the purpose and principles on which the financial statements are produced, and why and how marketers should focus on management accounting as the means for generating a more accurate portrait of the economic reality of the business. Design/methodology/approach We use a conceptual approach to investigate why external financial reports disregard the investment component of marketing and why this is unlikely to change. We examine the misalignment between marketing and financial accounting objectives, highlight issues on the marketing-accounting interface and suggest ways to address them. Findings We conclude that marketers' ambition to create a wider appreciation of the value they create is unlikely to be achieved through any changes to financial accounting rules in the foreseeable future. By focusing their efforts on financial accountants, rather than management accountants, marketers are looking for love in the wrong place. Practical implications We recommend marketers focus their efforts on management accounting, particularly in industries where marketing is a key driver of business performance, and suggest how to refocus. Originality/value This article explains how financial accounting provides a stylized representation of business performance that fails to adequately reflect marketing's contribution. It reveals the fallacy of believing that minor accounting changes can fix this issue, given conflicting interests and puts forward an alternative approach.

title: The Effect of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) on the Audit Efficiency of Selected Banks in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) on audit efficiency in selected banks in Nigeria, with emphasis on fraud detection and risk management. Audit efficiency was measured using average audit report lag. The study adopted an ex post facto research design and relied on secondary data obtained from published financial statements, annual reports, and regulatory disclosures of 10 selected banks in Nigeria for the period 2010 to 2025. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, while panel unit root tests were conducted to establish stationarity. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression analysis was then employed to test the effect of RPA-related variables on audit efficiency. The findings showed that RPA in fraud detection had a significant negative effect on audit report lag, indicating that automation enhances audit efficiency by reducing the time required to complete audit engagements. Furthermore, RPA in risk management, proxied by the average nonperforming loan ratio, is statistically significant effect on audit efficiency. The study concludes that RPA contributes more strongly to audit efficiency when applied to fraud detection than to risk management activities. The study recommends that banks increase investment in RPA-driven fraud detection systems and improve the integration of automation tools into their risk management frameworks. The study adds to existing knowledge on digital transformation, audit automation, and technology-enabled auditing in emerging economies.

title: The Role of Financial Technology Platforms in Expanding Financial Inclusion, Digital Banking Access, and Economic Participation in Rural Areas of China
summary: Objective The study asks what FinTech platforms contribute to financial inclusion and digital banking access in rural China, and whether that contribution reaches household economic participation. Methods Rural households are followed over time in a longitudinal panel, and the analysis stays quantitative and observational: no household is experimentally assigned to FinTech exposure. The Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index (PKU-DFIIC) proxies FinTech development, combining coverage breadth, usage depth and digitization level. Digital banking access and financial inclusion are built as mediators, so that the routes from FinTech to economic participation can be traced instead of assumed. Confounders at the household and regional levels are controlled throughout. Four estimators are brought together - fixed effects, mediation analysis, quantile regression and dynamic panel GMM - each answering a part of the causal question that the others cannot. Findings FinTech carries a coefficient of 0.406 (p < 0.001), which reads as a 0.406 rise in log household income for each additional unit of FinTech adoption once the other covariates are held fixed. Digital banking points the same way and is likewise significant, at 0.191 (p < 0.001). Among the financial variables, inclusion dominates: its coefficient of 0.300 (p < 0.001) is the largest, and so is its standardized beta of 0.339. Once digital financial indicators enter the model, most macroeconomic and household controls no longer register as statistically significant; whatever explanatory power they had appears to be absorbed by the digital financial measures. Conclusion What raises household economic participation is not digital finance as such, but the access to and use of formal financial services that it makes possible.

title: Benchmarking green operational capabilities in food-processing SMEs: motivation, innovation, knowledge and business sustainability performance
summary: Purpose This study benchmarks green operational capabilities (green motivation, green innovation and green knowledge management) against business sustainability performance in food-processing SMEs, identifying which capabilities constitute best-practice drivers and which represent performance gaps. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on data from 252 food-based SMEs in Greater Jakarta and employing covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM), the study tests how these capabilities influence green entrepreneurial behavior and sustainability performance. Findings Results reveal that green motivation and green innovation are high-performance benchmark capabilities that significantly drive entrepreneurial behavior and, in turn, sustainability outcomes. In contrast, green knowledge management is identified as an underperforming capability, exhibiting a knowledge–action gap in which environmental knowledge fails to translate into entrepreneurial behavior. A cross-firm benchmarking analysis further confirms that high-performing SMEs systematically outperform their peers on the motivational and innovation dimensions, whereas knowledge management scores do not differentiate performance clusters. Originality/value These findings contribute operational benchmarking insights for SME managers, industry associations, and policymakers seeking to prioritize capability investments for sustainability improvement.

summary: The fashion bag accessories industry in Indonesia has experienced rapid growth, driven by shifting consumer preferences, digital transformation, and increasing sustainability awareness. However, intensifying competition and the influx of low-cost imported products present significant challenges for local brands. This study aims to analyze the competitive dynamics of the industry using PEST analysis and Porter's Five Forces, and to identify how the integration of design innovation, digital branding, and sustainability contributes to competitive advantage. This research employs a qualitative descriptive approach using secondary data from industry reports, academic literature, and relevant case studies. The findings reveal that external factors, particularly technological advancements and socio-cultural changes, significantly influence industry dynamics, while internal capabilities play a crucial role in shaping firm competitiveness. Furthermore, many businesses still adopt fragmented strategies and have not yet effectively integrated innovation, digitalization, and sustainability. This study proposes an integrative strategic model that demonstrates how the alignment of design innovation, digital branding, and sustainability can strengthen competitive advantage. The findings provide both theoretical and practical contributions to the development of strategic management in the fashion accessories industry.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance, Komite Audit, Audit Fee Terhadap Kualitas Audit Pada Perusahaan Sektor Energi yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: ABSTRACT Audit quality is a key indicator of the reliability of a company's financial reports, which is increasingly critical amidst the complexity of energy sector business transactions. This study aims to examine the influence of good corporate governance (GCG), audit committees, and audit fees on audit quality in energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The research method used was quantitative with a purposive sampling technique, resulting in a sample of 15 companies for the 2022-2024 period, with a total of 45 observations. Secondary data was obtained through documentation of annual reports and financial statements published on the IDX. Data analysis used logistic regression with SPSS. The research results indicate that, individually, good corporate governance and the audit committee have a significant negative effect on audit quality, whereas audit fees have a significant positive effect. Collectively, good corporate governance, the audit committee, and audit fees have a significant impact on audit quality. The coefficient of determination shows that the variables of good corporate governance, the audit committee, and audit fees explain 72.1% of the variation in audit quality, while the remainder is influenced by factors outside the scope of this study. title: Agility and Flexibility Strategies in Manufacturing Systems: A Systematic Review with a Focus on Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: Special companies, those in markets with fluctuating demand and supply, need to take the ups and downs in the market, disruption in their supply chains, and the technology and competitive pressure, and still maintain delivery, quality, and cost targets. The present systematic review, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, aims at gathering 42 studies related to the manufacturing agility and flexibility, focusing on Sub Saharan Africa (SSA). The corpus consists of manufacturing flexibility, agile and leagile manufacturing, lean practice, supply-chain agility, digital transformation and Industry 4.0 and is segmented based on application domain, geography, methodology and publication period. The evidence suggests that agility and flexibility are associated with improved operational and organisational performance in SSA, but the pathways and degree of application varies significantly between firms and countries. The consistent challenges are cost, skills, infrastructure (reliability of power supply) and supply chain; management commitment is always cited as the final key. Digital technologies and Industry 4.0 are enablers that require a combination of infrastructure, organisational integration and human capability, and not just ownership of digital technology. There is some fragmentation in measurement of agility – different constructs are used in various surveys, there are formal agility indices, and new AI-assisted assessment frameworks are emerging – none of which have yet been validated for SSA. A series of shop-floor studies in Zimbabwe (process-parameter optimisation, data-driven maintenance, and agent-based condition monitoring) demonstrates that new capabilities at the operational level can be realized at relatively low costs, but are rarely related to the strategic agility literature. The conceptual framework and research agenda of the review call for a SSA-specific measurement tool, an integrated socio-technical model, operational as well as longitudinal evidence, and more robust mechanisms of building industry–academy capabilities, e.g., learning factories.

title: Empowering communities for environmental resilience through people centric strategies in natural resource management and sustainable rural development
summary: Environmental degradation, accelerating climate change, persistent rural poverty, and biodiversity loss represent some of the most pressing challenges confronting the global community today. These intertwined crises have intensified the urgent need for sustainable natural resource management (NRM) and rural development strategies that place communities at their center. In response, a marked paradigm shift has emerged from centralized, top-down governance towards people-centric, community-driven frameworks that recognize the indispensable role of local and Indigenous actors in stewarding natural resources and sustaining ecosystem services. Despite this growing recognition, the existing literature on Community-Based Natural Resource Management (CBNRM) remains largely context-specific and lacks comparative synthesis, while empirical analysis of participatory governance structures—particularly the vertical alignment of local, national, and international policy frameworks—remains limited. This study addresses these critical gaps through a systematic literature review (SLR) of 150 peer-reviewed journal articles published between January 2020 and May 2025, guided by the PRISMA and ROSES reporting frameworks, and employing thematic synthesis and comparative analysis to generate robust, transferable insights. This review seeks to answer three research questions: (1) How can the scaling of participatory natural resource management models be achieved? (2) What strategies can be employed for the integration of green innovation and the circular economy within rural and resource-dependent communities? (3) How do policy environments impact community participation in natural resource governance? The findings reveal that the application of CBNRM improves household livelihoods by 75% when tenure security is ensured and stakeholder engagement is facilitated. Green innovation is advanced through context-driven eco-innovation and waste-to-resource technologies, with circular agriculture emerging as a particularly effective mechanism for resource efficiency. Multi-level governance coordination is identified as essential for the effective implementation of environmental policies, while participatory policy development significantly outperforms conventional top-down approaches in achieving policy compliance and community buy-in. These findings underscore the imperative for integrated strategies that combine social capital development, adaptive governance, rights-based approaches, and transformative participation. The study makes a significant contribution to sustainable development scholarship by providing actionable, evidence-based frameworks for policymakers, practitioners, and development organizations seeking to empower communities as agents of environmental resilience in alignment with the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

title: Evolutionary transformation and ontology of logistics systems in the context of national economic development
summary: The article provides a theoretical and methodological generalization of the ontological foundations and chronological evolution of scientific thought on the formation and functioning of logistics systems within the national economy. Causal relationships and the systemic-evolutionary trajectory of logistics transformation – from performing fragmented operational-transportation and warehousing functions to building complex digital networks and macroeconomic ecosystems – are examined. The study systematizes and periodizes key stages in the development of logistics instruments amid modern digitalization, institutional transformations, and structural shifts in the macro-environment. The study substantiates the growing role of information and communication as a key strategic resource for management, forecasting, and coordinating flow processes at the micro-, meso-, and macroeconomic levels. The study identifies the essence of digital logistics, along with the tools of the platform-ecosystem approach (IoT, Big Data, AI, digital twins, data spaces), as the basis for ensuring stability, transparency, and macroeconomic resilience in logistics systems. The study proves the need to unify the information technology parameters of the national logistics infrastructure for full integration into international and European logistics data spaces. The modern paradigm of logistics support for the national economy is defined by large-scale digital transformation, which involves integrating the Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, digital twins, and unified data space technologies. Applying these tools shifts the focus from managing the purely physical movement of material resources to creating a highly integrated information and communication environment. Such an environment ensures the transparency, adaptability, and resilience of business entities and the national economy amid macroeconomic uncertainty and global challenges. Future research should focus on developing applied mechanisms for regulatory, institutional, and technological unification of domestic information and logistics systems to integrate them into international and European logistics data spaces fully. Keywords: logistics system, national economy, ontology of logistics, macrologistics, supply chains, digital logistics, data spaces, resilience.

title: Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure and Firm Performance: Evidence from Saudi Listed Firms
summary: The objective of this research is to find out if supply chain sustainability disclosure is related to firm performance among publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia. A unique and valid Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure Index (SCDI) that has six variables is measured based on the standards in the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) (2019) which are GRI 204, GRI 308, and GRI 414 through a systematic content analysis of 142 annual accounts of 58 publicly-listed non-financial corporations on the Saudi stock exchange (Tadawul) from 2022 to 2025. This study uses several panel regressions with fixed effects with respect to firm and year while using clustered standard errors of classified at the firm level. The study did not discover any evidence of a statistically significant connection between disclosure rates of the Supply Chain Sustainability Disclosure Index (SCDI) and firm performance measured by Return on Assets (ROA) or Return on Equity (ROE) taking into consideration various models such as main, lagged, ESG- alternative and restricted samples of the gathered data. The findings illustrate that the SCDI was found to be 0.11 while it had a median value of zero which indicates very little disclosure of Supply Chain sustainability. Therefore, it was concluded that in this window of opportunity and market, disclosure is mostly linked to the process of legitimation rather than performance-based signaling, due to the lack of variation among the gathered sample.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, GENDER DIVERSITY, DAN ESG DISCLOSURE: IMPLIKASI TERHADAP KINERJA PERUSAHAAN DAN KEBERLANJUTAN
summary: Corporate governance and gender diversity have become strategic factors in enhancing the effectiveness of ESG disclosure and integrated reporting (IR). This article presents a narrative literature review of 18 selected scientific articles published between 2019 and 2025, analyzed through a process of identification, screening, and relevance evaluation based on the research topics of corporate governance, gender diversity, and ESG disclosure. The reviewed literature examines the relationship between corporate governance practices, gender diversity on boards of directors and senior management, and the quality of ESG disclosure. The findings indicate that strong governance mechanisms and adequate gender diversity are positively associated with improved ESG disclosure quality and firm performance. Comprehensive ESG disclosure contributes to reducing the cost of capital, increasing firm value, and strengthening corporate reputation, particularly in the context of emerging markets. This article identifies research gaps related to the influence of local institutions, cultural contexts, and the adoption of digital technologies in supporting ESG disclosure, while providing practical implications for regulators and companies in strengthening sustainable business practices.
